title: Mentioning educational aspirations or learning via online tutorials may predict slower funding for female borrowers.
Female borrowers who include the loan amount in local currency may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers describing an existing business may fund faster than those describing starting a new one.
Female borrowers who explicitly state their age may fund more slowly.
Lengthier pitches may predict slower funding for female borrowers.
Mentioning home or living condition improvements accelerates funding for women but slows it for men.
Female borrowers who mention diversifying their income or product range may fund faster.
Explicitly stating marital status may predict slower funding for female borrowers.
Detailed daily routines may accelerate funding for male borrowers.
Mentioning family members and their roles may predict slower funding for male borrowers.
Mentioning specific institutional or brand names predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Explicit expressions of gratitude to lenders accelerate funding for female borrowers.
Male borrowers who specify the number of years the business has operated fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Mentioning benefits for children predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who explicitly mention their education level fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention business duration or loan history fund more slowly.
